solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise a financial centre's greed

parts.note: to rap someone is to criticise them sharply
the City is London's financial centre

explanation.surface: A rebuke aimed at the avarice of a banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, aggressive greed, a near synonym for avarice.

clue.text: Secret society disposing of leader in Marrakesh house

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is thrown away

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal secret society

explanation.surface: A secret society losing its boss in a house in Marrakesh, like a thriller plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A riad is a traditional Moroccan house built around a courtyard, common in Marrakesh.

clue.text: Owl, might one say: once an opponent of the king?

definitions.meaning: a group of owls is a parliament, so one owl is jokingly a member of it

definitions.text: once an opponent of the king

explanation.surface: Muses whether an owl was once one of the king's enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for owls is a parliament, and Parliamentarians were Roundheads opposing the Royalists.

clue.text: Bashful girl, they say, this Indian

indicators.note: they say means what follows is heard rather than written

parts.note: bashful is shy and Anne is a girl's name, giving shy Anne

explanation.surface: A timid girl is said to be of a Native American people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals that SHY ANNE is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains, an Indian nation in older usage.

clue.text: Food at back only half edible

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round to read the other way
only half the word is used, here its second three letters

explanation.surface: Food at the back of the fridge is only half fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AT into TA; 'only half' keeps BLE, the second half of EDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table.

clue.text: Israelite's manly drink?

definitions.note: used adjectivally: belonging to an Israelite, as Hebrew can mean

parts.note: manly suggests 'he' as in he-man, so HE
a brew is a drink, especially tea or beer

explanation.surface: Asks whether an ancient Israelite's drink is a macho one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew as an adjective describes the ancient Jewish people, so it means belonging to an Israelite.

clue.text: Wife that was cheeky and clever

parts.note: a former wife is an ex
pert means impudent or cheeky

explanation.surface: Describes a former wife as saucy and smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert as an adjective means highly skilled, a close sense of clever.

clue.text: Review fee for Bible class?

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
a consideration is a payment, a fee for services

explanation.surface: A review of what is charged for a Bible study group.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the school subject where British pupils study the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconsideration is a second look at something, a review.

clue.text: Weak policeman deserving prison

parts.note: wan means pale and feeble
DS is a detective sergeant
worth means meriting, deserving

explanation.surface: A feeble officer earns a stretch inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Wandsworth is a large men's prison in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: HMP Wandsworth is a well-known London jail, so the name stands for a prison.

clue.text: Ancient medal I've restored

indicators.note: restored means rebuilt, so the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: An old medal has been restored by the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval describes the Middle Ages, loosely used to mean very old or ancient.

clue.text: Sympathise with beer guzzling bishop in Nice

parts.note: to agree with someone is to share their view, to sympathise

indicators.note: the beer is pictured swallowing the bishop, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric drinking beer on holiday in the French city of Nice finds company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the end looks like the French resort; it is the plain adjective. 'guzzling' puts B inside ALE to give ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable describes something pleasant, a straightforward synonym of nice.

clue.text: Pie-maker about to be put in jail

indicators.note: the word for about is placed inside the word for jail

parts.note: pen is slang for a jail, short for penitentiary
CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A baker of pies is about to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie-maker' looks like a baker; it is the nut that goes into pecan pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecan pie is a classic American dessert, so the nut is what makes the pie.

clue.text: Cut Peter out, bring Charlie in

indicators.note: bring ... in tells us to insert the letter into the other word
completes bring ... in, putting C inside

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away, to die
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Instructions to drop one man, Peter, and bring in another, Charlie, like a team change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter out' looks like removing someone named Peter; it is the phrasal verb meaning fade, DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice vegetables is to cut them into small cubes.

clue.text: Settlers built grand minarets

indicators.note: the letters are put together into a new construction

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Newcomers to a land erected impressive mosque towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants leave home to settle elsewhere, so they become settlers in the new country.

clue.text: Poor female host Helen, lonely and unloved?

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor woman, Helen, is a hostess left lonely and unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges HOSTHELEN, then F for female ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the shelf is an idiom for being past the age of finding a partner, by example lonely and unloved.

clue.text: A case of resident saving no time at all?

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a native is a resident of a place
nought minutes: O for nothing plus MIN for minutes

explanation.surface: Asks whether a resident's legal case needs no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' puts O MIN inside NATIVE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The nominative is the grammatical case of a sentence's subject, as in Latin or German.

clue.text: Paintings returned — and poetry? It makes you cross

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: art means works such as paintings
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Pictures sent back with some poems annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ART into TRA. 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the verb meaning go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a place is to travel over or across it.

clue.text: Writer of panache newspaper advanced

indicators.note: advanced means pushed forward, so this letter moves earlier in the word

parts.note: brio is verve or panache
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A writer with flair was promoted at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' moves the I of BRIO one place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing implement, so a writer in the crossword sense.

clue.text: First two leaving subdued and tense

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters go away from the word

parts.note: restrained means held back, subdued

explanation.surface: Losing the top two players leaves a team quiet and on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained nerves or relations are tense, under pressure.

clue.text: Applause for royal flush?

definitions.meaning: 'give them a big ...' means applaud them
in poker a royal flush is the best possible ...

explanation.surface: Asks what earns cheering for a winning poker deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand means both a round of clapping and the cards a poker player holds, such as a royal flush.

clue.text: Way in which you might make money abroad

definitions.text: Way in which you might make money abroad

parts.words: Way in which you might make money abroad
parts.note: a street is a way, and this New York street is America's financial centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is not a method but a road; the street is in New York, hence 'abroad' for a British solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is the New York thoroughfare home to the stock exchange and big banks.

clue.text: Dawn and Victor in a hole

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for hole

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two people, Dawn and Victor, are stuck in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name paired with Victor; it means a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is an arrival or coming, the dawn of something new.

clue.text: Want dress jazzed up for swingers' club?

indicators.note: jazzing something up livens and rearranges it

explanation.surface: Wanting a flashy outfit for a risqué club for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swingers' looks racy; it means golfers swinging clubs. St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf and its Royal and Ancient Golf Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers swing, and St Andrews is the famous golf club, a witty twist on swingers.

clue.text: A doctor in South America listening to this?

indicators.note: these letters go inside the abbreviation for the continent

parts.note: SA is South America
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor in Brazil, perhaps, has this music playing.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is Brazilian dance music, the kind of tune a doctor in South America might hear.

clue.text: Proposal Athens rejected in part, sad to say

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Regretfully, a proposal made by Athens was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used to introduce unwelcome news.

clue.text: Escort booting out husband who's on drugs

indicators.note: kicking out means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: An escort agency drops a husband who takes drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs.

clue.text: Refugee finding foreign article in river

indicators.note: the article sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing finds a foreign object in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: IL is Italian for 'the', a definite article; the River Exe flows through Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone forced from their country, as a refugee is.

clue.text: Meaning of occasionally steamy goings-on?

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some letters, here every other one starting with the first

parts.note: antics are capers or goings-on

explanation.surface: Asks what is meant by some occasional racy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the study of meaning in language, and loosely the meaning of a word itself.

clue.text: It's all over for Benito Mussolini

definitions.text: It's all over for Benito Mussolini

parts.words: It's all over for Benito Mussolini
parts.note: Mussolini spoke Italian, so the end for him would be put in Italian

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the Italian dictator's own word for 'finished'.
explanation.definitionFit: Finito is Italian for finished, borrowed in English to mean all over.

clue.text: Can one forgive what's written by Her Majesty?

definitions.note: a noun phrase in disguise: one who can forgive

indicators.note: written by means the royal cipher is set down next to the first word, after it

parts.note: pardon? is the genteel way of saying what? when you have not heard
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Wonders whether it is possible to forgive something the Queen wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' is not a pronoun but the polite 'Pardon?' said instead of 'What?'. A pardoner sold papal pardons, as in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval pardoner was licensed to grant remission of sins, someone able to absolve.
